pr.title: Guard HIR lowered contracts with `contract_checks`
pr.description:
Refactor contract HIR lowering to ensure no contract code is executed when contract-checks are disabled.

The call to `contract_checks` is moved to inside the lowered fn body, and contract closures are built conditionally, ensuring no side-effects present in contracts occur when those are disabled. This partially addresses rust-lang/rust#139548, i.e. the bad behavior no longer happens with contract checks disabled (`-Zcontract-checks=no`).

The change is made in preparation for adding contract variable declarations - variables declared before the `requires` assertion, and accessible from both `requires` and `ensures`, but not in the function body (PR rust-lang/rust#144444). As those declarations may also have side-effects, it's good to guard them with `contract_checks` - the new lowering approach allows for this to be done easily.

Contracts tracking issue: rust-lang/rust#128044

**Known limiatations**:

- It is still possible to early return from the *function* from within a contract, e.g.

  ```rust
  #[ensures({if x > 0 { return 0 }; |_| true})]
  fn foo(x: u32) -> i32 {
      42
  }
  ```

  When `foo` is called with an argument greater than 0, instead of `42`, `0` will be returned.

  As this is not a regression, it is not addressed in this PR. However, it may be worth revisiting later down the line, as users may expect a form of early return from *contract specifications*, and so returning from the entire *function* could cause confusion.

- ~Contracts are still not optimised out when disabled. Currently, even when contracts are disabled, the code generated causes existing optimisations to fail, meaning even disabled contracts could impact runtime performance. This issue is blocking rust-lang/rust#136578, and has not been addressed in this PR, i.e. the `mir-opt` and `codegen` tests that fail in rust-lang/rust#136578 still fail with these new HIR lowering changes.~ Contracts should now be optimised out when disabled, however some regressions tests still need to be added to be sure that is indeed the case.
pr.author: dawidl022

analysis.originalLogic: Before the PR, contract HIR lowering in `compiler/rustc_ast_lowering/src/item.rs` emitted the `requires` check and the `ensures` checker declaration unconditionally before the function body, then wrapped body returns with `contract_check_ensures` unconditionally. Runtime gating was delegated to the `contract_checks()` intrinsic: `LowerIntrinsics` lowered `sym::contract_checks` to `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::ContractChecks, tcx.types.bool)`, and `contract_check_requires`/`contract_check_ensures` tested `contract_checks()` before panicking. Thus the contract expressions and ensures checker closure were still constructed/executed when checks were disabled.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically incorrect lowering: keep unconditional construction of contract code in the HIR body and guard only the final runtime check via the `contract_checks()` intrinsic. With `-Zcontract-checks=no`, a side effect performed while evaluating a `requires` expression or while building/capturing the `ensures` closure still executes. The corrected transformation instead lowers the compiler flag into a literal HIR boolean guard (`self.tcx.sess.contract_checks()`) so contract code is placed inside `if contract_checks { ... } else { ... }`; the ensures checker is represented as `Option<C>`, with `Some(closure)` built only in the enabled branch and `None` in the disabled branch. The `contract_checks` intrinsic, its type-check entry, and its `LowerIntrinsics` arm are removed.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions annotated with `#[requires(...)]` and/or `#[ensures(...)]` under `#![feature(contracts)]`, especially contract expressions or ensures closures whose evaluation/construction has side effects (mutation, function calls, captured state). Compare compilation with `-Zcontract-checks=no` versus `-Zcontract-checks=yes`, including requires-only, ensures-only, and both. Also relevant: cross-crate calls where the dependency crate's contract-check setting differs from the caller's, and MIR containing calls to the `contract_checks` intrinsic.
analysis.summary: Bug-fix knowledge for contract lowering: do not merely gate the contract panic at runtime; guard construction/evaluation of contract code itself with the compile-time contract-checks flag. The historical implementation built precondition expressions and ensures-checker closures unconditionally and used `contract_checks()`/`NullOp::ContractChecks` only inside the check intrinsic, so side effects ran even with `-Zcontract-checks=no`. The fix lowers `tcx.sess.contract_checks()` to an HIR boolean literal guard, builds the ensures checker as `Option<C>` (Some only when enabled), and removes the `contract_checks` intrinsic and its LowerIntrinsics lowering arm.
analysis.trigger: Compile a function with contracts using `-Zcontract-checks=no` where the contract expression or ensures closure has an observable side effect. Historical lowering executed that side effect because the contract code was emitted before the body and only the final check was gated by `contract_checks()`. A representative trigger is an `#[ensures({*x = 0; |_ret| true})]` contract whose mutation runs even when checks are disabled.
preconditions: The function is annotated with `#[requires(...)]` and/or `#[ensures(...)]` under `#![feature(contracts)]`.
The contract expression or ensures closure construction has an observable side effect (for example, mutating a reference argument during closure capture).
The crate is compiled with contract checks disabled, e.g. `-Zcontract-checks=no`.
The lowered MIR previously contained a `contract_checks` intrinsic call lowered by LowerIntrinsics to `NullOp::ContractChecks`; after the fix that intrinsic and lowering arm are gone.
pitfalls: Guarding only the panic/check call is insufficient: side effects happen while evaluating the `requires` expression or constructing/capturing the `ensures` closure, so the construction itself must be inside the disabled/enabled branch.

The `ensures` checker must be optional (`Option<C>`): `None` when checks are disabled prevents constructing the closure, while `Some(closure)` is built only when enabled. The intrinsic signature and caller were both updated accordingly.
Do not remove contract code entirely from HIR when checks are disabled; the PR deliberately keeps it type-checked and relies on the optimizer to eliminate `if false` code, avoiding stale contracts.

Removing the `contract_checks` intrinsic must be coordinated across its core definition, intrinsic type-checking, and the `LowerIntrinsics` match arm; leaving any one behind creates stale references or dead lowering logic.
Do not conflate runtime panic gating with side-effect gating. `-Zcontract-checks=no` must suppress both the panic and all side effects from contract code.
The known early-return limitation remains: a `return` inside a contract still returns from the whole function, not just the contract specification.
Cross-crate behavior is independent: a dependency may be compiled with contract checks enabled even when the caller is compiled with them disabled; the test matrix covers all four combinations.
analysis.testStrategy: Add UI/run-pass tests for contract side effects with `-Zcontract-checks=no`, asserting the body's result is unaffected; the patch adds `tests/ui/contracts/contracts-disabled-side-effect-ensures.rs` with `#[ensures({*x = 0; |_ret| true})]` and `assert_eq!(x, 110);`. Exercise revision matrices for requires-only, ensures-only, and both with `-Zcontract-checks=no` and `=yes`; the patch's cross-crate test (`tests/ui/contracts/cross-crate-checks/`) covers dependency/caller flag combinations. Update internal-intrinsic tests to pass `Some(closure)` to `contract_check_ensures` and verify `None` skips checking. Add MIR/codegen checks that `if false`-guarded contracts are optimized out. Include compile-fail coverage for empty `#[requires()]`/`#[ensures()]` because the macro delimiters changed from parentheses to braces. No compiler was built here, so do not claim these tests were executed.
evidence: Refactor contract HIR lowering to ensure no contract code is executed when contract-checks are disabled.
The call to `contract_checks` is moved to inside the lowered fn body, and contract closures are built conditionally, ensuring no side-effects present in contracts occur when those are disabled.
The optimiser should be able to eliminate all contract code guarded
If `cond` is `None`, then no postcondition checking is performed.
It is still possible to early return from the *function* from within a contract
